extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in PTAB inter partes review (Petitioner and Patent Owner) and practitioners appearing before the Board
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, filing deadlines, and practice requirements governing an inter partes review before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including conference-call procedures, protective order rules, testimony and cross-examination timing, motion-to-amend practice, oral-argument procedures, and due-date-specific filing permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and additional conference call requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties are directed to contact the Board within a month of this Order if there is a need to discuss proposed changes to this Scheduling Order or proposed motions that have not been authorized in this Order or other prior Order or Notice. A request for an initial conference call shall include a list of proposed motions, if any, to be discussed during the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any email requesting a conference call with the Board should: (a) copy all parties, (b) indicate generally the relief being requested or the subject matter of the conference call, (c) include multiple times when all parties are available, (d) state whether the opposing party opposes any relief requested, and (e) if opposed, either certify that the parties have met and conferred telephonically or in person to attempt to reach agreement, or explain why such meet and confer did not occur. The email may not contain substantive argument and, unless otherwise authorized, may not include attachments. See Consolidated Practice Guide at 9–10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective order and sealing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: No protective order shall apply to this proceeding until the Board enters one. If either party files a motion to seal before entry of a protective order, a jointly proposed protective order shall be filed as an exhibit with the motion. It is the responsibility of the party whose confidential information is at issue ... to file the motion to seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board encourages use of the Board’s default protective order. If parties propose a protective order deviating from the default, they must submit the proposed protective order jointly along with a marked-up comparison showing differences and explain why good cause exists to deviate. Redactions to documents should be limited to the minimum necessary to protect confidential information, and the thrust of the underlying argument or evidence must be clearly discernible from redacted versions. Information subject to a protective order may become public if identified in a final written decision; a motion to expunge may not prevail over public interest in a complete record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery disputes — meet-and-confer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board encourages parties to resolve disputes relating to discovery on their own. To the extent that a dispute arises between the parties relating to discovery, the parties must meet and confer to resolve such a dispute before contacting the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If attempts to resolve the dispute fail, a party may request a conference call with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Testimony Guidelines and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Testimony Guidelines appended to the Consolidated Practice Guide at 127–130 (App. D, Testimony Guidelines) apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may impose an appropriate sanction for failure to adhere to the Testimony Guidelines (37 C.F.R. § 42.12). For example, reasonable expenses and attorneys’ fees incurred by any party may be levied on a person who impedes, delays, or frustrates the fair examination of a witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as the parties might otherwise agree, for each due date: Cross-examination ordinarily takes place after any supplemental evidence is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination ordinarily ends no later than a week before the filing date for any paper in which the cross-examination testimony is expected to be used. See 37 C.F.R. § 42.53(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend — conference call and pre-filing conferral
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner may file a motion to amend without prior authorization from the Board. Nevertheless, Patent Owner must confer with the Board before filing such a motion (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(a)). To satisfy this requirement, Patent Owner should request a conference call with the Board no later than two weeks prior to DUE DATE 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner has option to receive preliminary guidance from the Board on its motion to amend (per MTA Pilot Program Notice). If Patent Owner elects to request preliminary guidance, it must do so in its motion to amend filed on DUE DATE 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend — procedural framework and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend and briefing related to such a motion shall generally follow the practices and procedures described in the MTA Pilot Program Notice unless otherwise ordered by the Board in this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties directed to relevant precedent (Lectrosonics v. Zaxcom) and the Rules of Practice To Allocate the Burden of Persuasion on Motions To Amend. At DUE DATE 3, Patent Owner may file a reply to the opposition to the motion to amend and preliminary guidance, or a revised motion to amend. A revised motion to amend must provide amendments, arguments, and/or evidence in a manner that is responsive to issues raised in the preliminary guidance and/or Petitioner’s opposition. If Patent Owner files a revised motion to amend, the Board will enter a revised scheduling order setting briefing for that revised motion and adjusting other due dates as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to Board preliminary guidance (MTA Pilot) — reply/sur-reply timing and evidence restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: As discussed in the MTA Pilot Program Notice, if the Board issues preliminary guidance on the motion to amend, and Patent Owner files neither a reply to the opposition to the motion to amend nor a revised motion to amend at DUE DATE 3, Petitioner may file a reply to the Board’s preliminary guidance, no later than three (3) weeks after DUE DATE 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply may only respond to the preliminary guidance. Patent Owner may file a sur-reply in response to Petitioner’s reply to the Board’s preliminary guidance; the sur-reply may only respond to arguments made in the reply and must be filed no later than three (3) weeks after Petitioner’s reply. No new evidence may accompany the reply or the sur-reply in this situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument request rules and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for oral argument must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 42.70(a). To permit the Board sufficient time to schedule the oral argument, the parties may not stipulate to an extension of the request for oral argument beyond the date set forth in the Due Date Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may request the oral argument be held at USPTO headquarters or virtually by videoconference. Parties should state in the request (DUE DATE 4) whether they prefer video or in-person; if parties disagree they should meet and confer and, if unresolved, inform the Board of each party’s preferences. PTAB will only conduct an in-person hearing when requested by all parties. Board may not be able to honor preferences due to hearing-room resources, panel needs, or USPTO policy. For in-person hearings, seating may be limited and is first-come, first-served. If either party anticipates more than five individuals attending on its behalf, the party should notify the Board no later than the request for oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP program participation and extra argument time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board established the LEAP program to encourage development of advocates; a LEAP practitioner is defined as a patent agent or attorney having three (3) or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal, including PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will grant up to fifteen (15) minutes of additional argument time to that party, depending on the length of the proceeding and the PTAB’s hearing schedule. A party should submit a request, no later than at least five (5) business days before the oral hearing, by email to PTABHearings@uspto.gov. A LEAP Verification Form shall be submitted by the LEAP practitioner confirming eligibility; a combined Request and Verification Form is available at www.uspto.gov/leap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards for practitioners at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: All practitioners appearing before the Board shall demonstrate the highest professional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are expected to have a command of the factual record, the applicable law, and Board procedures, as well as the authority to commit the party they represent. The Board notes that LEAP practitioners often have the best understanding of the facts and evidence and encourages their participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulation rules for moving due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties may stipulate different dates for DUE DATES 1, 5, and 6, as well as portions of DUE DATE 2 related to Petitioner’s reply and portions of DUE DATE 3 related to Patent Owner’s sur-reply, subject to limits noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may not stipulate to a different date for the portion of DUE DATE 2 related to Petitioner’s opposition to a motion to amend, or for the portion of DUE DATE 3 related to Patent Owner’s reply to an opposition to a motion to amend (or revised motion to amend) without prior authorization from the Board. In stipulating changed due dates, parties must consider effects on times to object to evidence (37 C.F.R. § 42.64(b)(1)), to supplement evidence (§ 42.64(b)(2)), to conduct cross-examination (§ 42.53(d)(2)), and to draft papers depending on the evidence and cross-examination testimony. A notice of the stipulation, specifically identifying the changed due dates, must be promptly filed. The parties may not stipulate an extension of DUE DATES 4, 7, and 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 1 filings and waiver warning
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 1: Patent Owner’s response to the petition and Patent Owner’s motion to amend the patent may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Patent Owner elects not to file a response, Patent Owner must arrange a conference call with the parties and the Board. Patent Owner is cautioned that any arguments not raised in the response may be deemed waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 2 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 2: Petitioner may file a reply to Patent Owner’s response to the petition and may file an opposition to the motion to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portions of DUE DATE 2 relating to Petitioner’s reply may be stipulated earlier or later (but no later than DUE DATE 3 for Patent Owner’s sur-reply), subject to the stipulation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 3 filings and options
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 3: Patent Owner may file a sur-reply to Petitioner’s reply and may file either (a) a reply to the opposition to the motion to amend and/or preliminary guidance (if provided), or (b) a revised motion to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Patent Owner files neither of the above papers and the Board has issued preliminary guidance, Petitioner may file a reply to the preliminary guidance no later than three (3) weeks after DUE DATE 3, and Patent Owner may file a sur-reply to Petitioner’s reply no later than three (3) weeks after Petitioner’s reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 4 — request for oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 4: Either party may file a request for oral argument (request may not be extended by stipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See oral argument rules (37 C.F.R. § 42.70(a)) and requirements for indicating in-person vs video preference when requesting argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 5 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 5: Petitioner may file a sur-reply to Patent Owner’s reply to the opposition to the motion to amend. Either party may file a motion to exclude evidence (37 C.F.R. § 42.64(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should consider effect on subsequent deadlines and cross-examination scheduling when using these filing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 6 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 6: Either party may file an opposition to a motion to exclude evidence and either party may request that the Board hold a pre-hearing conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may also use this date to request procedural conferences with the Board as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 7 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 7: Either party may file a reply to an opposition to a motion to exclude evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DUE DATE 7 may not be extended by stipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUE DATE 8 — oral argument date
rubrics_metrics.description: DUE DATE 8: The oral argument (if requested by either party) shall be held on this date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately one month prior to the argument, the Board will issue an order setting the start time of the hearing and the procedures that will govern the parties’ arguments. DUE DATE 8 may not be extended by stipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting/content limits on replies related to preliminary guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies and sur-replies that are filed in response to Board preliminary guidance may only respond to the preliminary guidance and may not include new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, if Petitioner replies to preliminary guidance, the reply may only respond to the preliminary guidance, and any Patent Owner sur-reply may only respond to arguments made in that reply. No new evidence may accompany the reply or sur-reply in this situation (MTA Pilot Program Notice at 9502).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and content of stipulations changing due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When parties stipulate to change due dates allowed by this Order, a notice of the stipulation, specifically identifying the changed due dates, must be promptly filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must be cognizant of the Board’s need for four weeks after filing of an opposition to a motion to amend for the Board to issue preliminary guidance (if requested). Consider effects on times to object to evidence, supplement evidence, conduct cross-examination, and drafting of papers.
